questions.q: What distinguishes a secondary ledger from a reporting currency?
options: A reporting currency is independent; a secondary ledger is just a currency conversion
They are two names for the same structure
A secondary ledger is an independent set of books; a reporting currency just restates the primary ledger in another currency
A secondary ledger can only be used for statistics, never for accounting balances
questions.explain: A secondary ledger is its own ledger, potentially with a different COA or method. A reporting currency is not independent — it mirrors the primary ledger's structure in another currency.

questions.q: What does the natural account segment qualifier do?
options: Identifies intercompany transactions
Classifies a value as asset, liability, equity, revenue, or expense
Controls which ledger a journal posts to
Restricts data access by business unit
questions.explain: The natural account segment drives financial statement classification — asset, liability, equity, revenue, or expense.

questions.q: Which work area would you use to create and post a manual journal?
options: Period Close
Scheduled Processes
Financial Reporting Center
Journals
questions.explain: The Journals work area is where manual journals are created, managed, approved, and posted.

questions.q: Why does the source/category combination matter beyond labeling?
options: It has no real functional impact
It only affects how a journal looks when printed
It determines the ledger's functional currency
Later features like approval rules and auto-post criteria sets commonly target specific source/category combinations
questions.explain: Approval rules, auto-post criteria, and suspense account rules are commonly scoped to specific source/category pairs.

questions.q: What is the difference between Save and Complete/Submit for a journal?
options: Save posts the journal; Complete deletes it
They are identical actions with different labels
Save stores a draft you can keep editing; Complete marks it ready to post or route for approval
Save requires approval; Complete does not
questions.explain: Save keeps a journal as an editable draft. Complete/Submit moves it toward posting or approval.

questions.q: Which of the following must be true before a journal can post?
options: It must have a control total entered
It must have passed validation, cleared any required approval, and have an accounting date in an Open period
It must use the Manual source
It must belong to a secondary ledger
questions.explain: Posting eligibility requires validation, approval clearance (if applicable), and an Open-status accounting date.

questions.q: In a parallel assignee routing, what is required for the journal to move forward?
options: Only one of the assigned people needs to approve
Approvers must act one after another in sequence
Everyone in the parallel set must approve
No approval is ever required
questions.explain: Parallel assignees all work at once, and every one of them must approve.

questions.q: What kind of discrepancy might legitimately trigger suspense posting on an interfaced journal?
options: A missing approval signature
An intentional duplicate entry
A small rounding or timing difference from an upstream system
A change in the ledger's chart of accounts
questions.explain: Suspense posting is typically used for small out-of-balance amounts caused by rounding or timing issues from interfaced sources.

questions.q: In the lesson's example, what caused Solara Fixtures' monthly allocation batch to post automatically?
options: A controller manually clicked Post
It was imported via FBDI
It was flagged for auto-reverse
It matched a criteria set (source Allocation, category Allocation, balance type Actual) and validated cleanly
questions.explain: The batch matched the defined criteria set's source, category, and balance type, triggering automatic posting.

questions.q: When would Formula be a better choice than Skeleton for a recurring entry?
options: When the amount never changes at all
When the amount is derivable from data already in the ledger, removing manual calculation
When no accounts are fixed
When the journal needs to skip validation
questions.explain: Formula is ideal when the amount can be computed from existing balances or statistics rather than manually calculated and typed.

questions.q: What is one way to handle a period where a recurring entry genuinely shouldn't run?
options: Generate it anyway and manually delete the batch afterward
Change its journal category to Adjustment
Simply don't generate it for that period, or give the definition an end date
Disable the entire ledger for that period
questions.explain: Skipping generation for that period, or ending the definition, avoids creating a batch that would need cleanup.

questions.q: What is the core allocation formula?
options: Cost Pool divided by number of periods
Total Usage divided by Cost Pool
Usage Factor multiplied by Total Usage
Cost Pool multiplied by (Target's Usage Factor divided by Total Usage)
questions.explain: Each target's share is the cost pool times its usage factor divided by total usage across all targets.

questions.q: What does the General Ledger Trial Balance Report fundamentally confirm?
options: That every account was coded to the correct cost center
That total debits equal total credits across the ledger's accounts for the selected period
That the chart of accounts has no inactive segments
That all subledger transactions have been imported
questions.explain: The historical and functional purpose of a trial balance is to confirm debits equal credits before proceeding toward close.

questions.q: Why would an auditor check a sequence-based report on document numbers for manual journals?
options: To calculate currency exchange rates
To approve budget transfers
To confirm completeness — that no document number in the sequence is missing
To reconcile bank statements
questions.explain: Sequence-based review confirms no manual journal document number is missing, a common completeness check in audits.

questions.q: From Account Inspector, which further actions are possible on the data?
options: None, it is a read-only dead end
Only exporting to a spreadsheet
Viewing the data as a chart and drilling in either direction, including down to journal lines and subledger transactions
Only changing the chart of accounts structure
questions.explain: Account Inspector supports charting the data and drilling from any parent or child level down to detail balances, journal lines, and subledger transactions.

questions.q: Which rate is used to translate balance sheet accounts, and why?
options: The period average rate, because balance sheet accounts accumulate over the whole period
The period-end spot rate, because a balance sheet is a snapshot as of that date
The original transaction-date rate, never updated
There is no rate used for balance sheet accounts
questions.explain: Because a balance sheet reflects a single point in time, it is translated using the period-end spot rate.

questions.q: Why can't consolidated entity balances simply be added together once they're in the consolidation ledger?
options: Because addition is not supported in Oracle Fusion
Because intercompany transactions between entities in the group would be double-counted unless eliminated
Because currencies cannot be combined under any circumstances
Because only one entity's balances are ever included
questions.explain: Transactions between group entities (debt, revenue/expense, stock ownership) represent the group dealing with itself and must be eliminated, not simply summed.

questions.q: What is the "entered currency amount" on a foreign currency journal line?
options: The amount converted to the ledger's functional currency
The amount as it actually occurred, in the original real-world transaction currency
A budgeted amount for comparison purposes only
The amount after year-end close adjustments
questions.explain: The entered amount preserves the real-world transaction exactly as it happened, in its original currency.

questions.q: Why are key system accounts like Accounts Payable control or Intercompany accounts specifically reviewed during close?
options: Because they are never affected by any journal
Because they should normally only move through subledger or intercompany processes, so a stray ad hoc manual journal hitting them is a red flag
Because they only exist in foreign currency ledgers
Because they are deleted automatically at year-end
questions.explain: These control accounts are expected to move only through their normal process (e.g., subledger posting), so unexpected manual journal activity there needs investigation.

questions.q: In the LTV Manufacturing Corporation example, FY2026 net income is $412,000. What happens when January 2027 opens?
options: Retained Earnings decreases by $412,000 and expense accounts double
Nothing changes until a user manually posts a journal
The $412,000 is deleted from the ledger entirely
Retained Earnings increases by $412,000 and every revenue/expense account opens at zero
questions.explain: The net income for the closed year sweeps automatically into Retained Earnings, and income statement accounts begin the new year at zero.

questions.q: What course comes next after General Ledger in the Oracle Fusion Financials Consultant path's Financials Configuration stage?
options: Oracle Fusion Cash Management
Oracle Fusion Security
SQL for Oracle Financials
Accounts Payable
questions.explain: Accounts Payable is next in the Financials Configuration stage, following Enterprise Structures & Chart of Accounts and General Ledger.
